articles.title: On why YC Series A rounds fell off a cliff
articles.summary: Series A rounds for Y Combinator startups have drastically declined since 2023, linked to a broader market downturn caused by rising interest rates. The downturn affected all YC batches, regardless of founder quality or admission year, as global early-stage funding fell sharply. Recent signs show a recovery, but raising Series A may become less necessary due to advancements in AI and increased focus on capital efficiency.

articles.title: Stripe's New Index Shows Non-AI B2B Revenue Up 30%+ Year Over Year Through the SaaSpocalypse
articles.summary: Software stocks lost an estimated $2 trillion early this year on fears that AI would replace business apps. Stripe's new weekly index of non-AI software companies that bill through it shows revenue up more than 30% from a year ago. Most of those companies sell self-serve products paid by card, and few of them are the enterprise names whose stocks fell. A company that shuts down also drops out of the index instead of counting as a loss. The index says little about enterprise seat pricing, so watch public companies' net revenue retention for that.

articles.title: Brand as Infrastructure
articles.summary: In-house designers keep getting requests to remake the same decks and one-pagers for other teams. Ramp's brand team handed that work to a Slack agent that builds them from approved examples the designers make in Figma. Automated tests catch broken layouts and missing fonts before anything goes back to the person who asked. One contractor automated about 90% of the company's whitepaper work in her second week. The designers now spend their time on work nobody has made yet, and each new hand-made deck goes back into the system as an example.

articles.title: Even the best technology won't achieve widespread adoption if its value isn't legible to both technologists and buyers.
articles.summary: Learn how to sell your product before hiring an executive to scale sales. Founders need to understand how customers make purchasing decisions and translate technical capabilities into value that both technologists and buyers recognize. Selling has become monotonous and repeatable, with more opportunities than the founder can handle alone.

articles.title: Linked billing on the Claude Platform (Tool)
articles.summary: Anthropic's new linked billing lets tools like Linear and Warp charge Claude usage to a customer's own Anthropic account, so nobody has to share an API key. Customers set a monthly spend limit for each linked tool and can unlink it at any time. Platforms decide on each request whether they or the customer pays. Linked billing is in beta now.

articles.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales
articles.summary: ChatGPT for Sales helps sales teams understand customers better, spend less time on busywork, and close more deals. It uses information from the tools teams already rely on to prepare for calls, tailor proposals, and follow up faster. The new Sales plugin from OpenAI provides ready-to-use workflows for everyday sales work, giving teams more time to make informed decisions and follow through on customer commitments. Availability of partner plugins will vary by plan, region, and workplace settings.

articles.title: AWS announces agentic account creation for agentic coding harnesses
articles.summary: Agent coding harness can now open the new AWS sign-up experience for developers who don't have an account. The default project setup comes with a home Region, IAM role manager, and short-term credentials that refresh automatically. Install the AWS plugin or configure the AWS Agent Toolkit in your agentic coding harness to try the new experience.

articles.title: ROI on IRL Events?
articles.summary: Events are a marketing and brand motion that educates people on your brand before they decide to do business with you. They are a great way to engage with existing customers and clients. Engaging socially with prospects is a much warmer experience for them, and it allows you to establish an initial dialogue. Events will increase your odds of setting up follow-up meetings and ultimately get new customers. To measure ROI, do a survey of attendees and track which customers attended the event.

articles.title: Lessons learned from commercializing dev infrastructure
articles.summary: Plenty of developer tools give away the core product and plan to charge for a faster managed version. Earthly did that with its build tool, and developers adopted it while few of them paid. Teams could get most of the speed by keeping their own build machines running, so the paid runners had little left to sell. Earthly shut that business down in 2025 and now sells automated checks for engineering standards to leaders who control the budget. Check whether your free version already delivers the value you plan to charge for.

articles.summary: Apps can show value before the paywall, like a personalized weight-loss projection, so define that value before debating where to charge.

articles.title: The First Order Is Curiosity. The Second Order Is Truth
articles.summary: A first purchase only proves someone was curious, so judge product-market fit by how many customers buy a second time.
